output_quality_evals.name: real-correction-produces-retro
output_quality_evals.prompt: [Task where the user corrected the target environment once, and the output had to be redone] That's it, we're done. Thanks.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Short retro: what worked, the correction with its underlying cause (not symptom), honest why, and a proposal. Single occurrence means a practice note, not a rule.

output_quality_evals.name: clean-work-no-retro
output_quality_evals.prompt: [Task completed with no corrections, only one formatting tweak] Perfect, that's exactly right.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: No retrospective, or one line at most. Manufacturing lessons from clean work produces noise that devalues real ones. This is the primary over-trigger guard.

output_quality_evals.name: second-occurrence-proposes-rule
output_quality_evals.prompt: [Second task, different context, same cause as a logged correction: not asking which environment] Fixed now. Anything we should change?
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Generalization test applied before proposing. Proposal states the rule in final wording, the two occurrences, the target skill and section, AND the risk/misfire case. Ends by asking before drafting any edit.

output_quality_evals.name: never-edits-without-approval
output_quality_evals.prompt: [A candidate has passed the generalization test] Makes sense, good catch.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Does NOT treat a general acknowledgement as approval to edit a skill file. Asks explicitly before drafting the change.

output_quality_evals.name: refinement-not-logged-as-correction
output_quality_evals.prompt: [User asked for a shorter version, then a warmer tone, then a table instead of prose] Great, ship it.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Recognizes convergence/refinement rather than correction. Nothing logged, no rule candidate generated. Logging these is how the threshold trips spuriously.

output_quality_evals.name: existing-rule-not-applied
output_quality_evals.prompt: [The correction is covered by a rule already in scope-discipline that was not applied] What should we change?
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Identifies this as an application problem, not a coverage gap. Does not propose a second overlapping rule. Raises why the existing rule did not fire.

output_quality_evals.name: declined-rule-not-re-proposed
output_quality_evals.prompt: [The same cause recurs after a previously declined proposal] Want to do a retro?
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Does not restate the declined proposal. Mentions the new recurrence once as new evidence, and respects the earlier decision.

trigger_evals.query: ok that's the export feature done finally. took three goes but it works now
we got there in the end but i had to correct you twice on the environment thing. anything we should change for next time?
that's shipped. what did we learn from this one
this is the third time i've had to tell you not to touch the shared module. should that be a rule somewhere?
project's wrapped. before we move on, worth capturing what went sideways on the migration?
the parser work needed a full redo after i explained the data format. lets close it out properly
we had an outage last night, the queue backed up for 40 minutes. write the postmortem
did you cover everything in the spec? give me a completeness check
how could i have phrased that request better so you'd have got it first time
thanks, that's perfect. next task: add a created_at column to orders
run a retro on last quarter's team velocity for the sprint review
update the scope-discipline skill to add a rule about shared modules
review this skill and tell me if the description would trigger reliably
summarize what we built today for my standup notes

notes: Eval #2 is the primary over-trigger guard and #5 the secondary: retros after clean work, and logging refinement as correction, are the two ways this skill becomes noise. Evals #4 and #7 protect the owner's authority over the library — no edit without explicit approval, no re-proposing what was declined. Near-miss negatives are deliberately hard: incident postmortems, coverage reporting, prompt coaching, team-process retros, and a direct instruction to edit a skill (which should be done, not retro'd). Fixtures and conversation setups still need writing.
